question: A team writes a /deploy skill that pushes to production. They want to guarantee Claude never triggers this skill on its own judgment during a normal conversation, while still letting any team member type /deploy to run it intentionally. Which frontmatter field accomplishes this?
options: A) context: fork, which runs the skill in an isolated subagent so the main conversation cannot decide to invoke it automatically.
B) user-invocable: false, which hides the skill from the / menu so Claude becomes the only party able to invoke it during a session.
C) allowed-tools: none, which strips every tool from the skill so Claude cannot act on it even if the skill content loads into context.
D) disable-model-invocation: true, which removes the skill's description from Claude's context so only a typed /deploy invocation can trigger it.
correct_answers: D) disable-model-invocation: true, which removes the skill's description from Claude's context so only a typed /deploy invocation can trigger it.
explanations: Incorrect. context: fork controls where the skill executes (a subagent versus inline) and has no effect on whether Claude can auto-invoke it.
Incorrect. user-invocable: false does the opposite of what's needed here: it prevents users from typing /deploy while leaving Claude free to invoke it automatically.
Incorrect. allowed-tools is not a valid value of none and controls pre-approved tool access, not who can trigger the skill.
Correct. disable-model-invocation: true keeps the skill's description out of Claude's context entirely, so only a direct /deploy invocation by a user can trigger it.
